title: On the difference between updating a knowledge base and revising it
abstract: Distinguishes revision, where new information changes beliefs about a static world, from update, where the represented world itself has changed. The distinction is directly relevant to separating corrections of prior assessments from genuine event or work-item state transitions.

title: Towards Generative Event Factuality Prediction
abstract: Introduces an end-to-end generative formulation that predicts factuality holders, factuality targets, and associated factuality values rather than assuming only the document author as source. Experiments use all sources and targets represented in FactBank and explore multitask learning with other factuality corpora.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023

title: An Empirical Characterization of Event Sourced Systems and Their Schema Evolution -- Lessons from Industry
abstract: Empirically studies event-sourced systems and how practitioners preserve and evolve event histories. It identifies schema-evolution strategies including versioned events, weak schemas, upcasting, in-place transformation, and copy-and-transform, providing engineering evidence for immutable history and state reconstruction.

title: Agreement, Disputes and Commitments in Dialogue
abstract: Provides a formal analysis of dialogue in which each participant has public commitments, including commitments to rhetorical or relational speech acts such as Correction. Agreement is defined through shared entailments, while the framework also gives consistent interpretations to disputes and to what remains agreed after disagreement.

title: Resolution of time concepts in temporal databases
abstract: Distinguishes event time, valid time, and transaction time and analyzes their roles in precise preservation of temporal information. The paper argues that event time is needed for retroactive and proactive updates and shows how multiple time dimensions preserve past states through error corrections, delayed updates, and other changes.

title: Layered message semantics using social commitments
abstract: Defines agent messages as coordinating devices that advance conversations, social commitments, and joint activities. Its commitment model includes lifecycle states such as accepted, rejected, active, fulfilled, violated, inactive, and cancelled, with messages interpreted partly through the commitment-state transitions they induce.

title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
abstract: Formalizes provenance for data created through database queries and distinguishes why-provenance, identifying source data that influenced an output, from where-provenance, identifying source locations from which output values originated. The distinction supplies foundational machinery for retaining evidential lineage instead of only final values.

title: The Problem of Retraction in Critical Discussion
abstract: Examines how dialogue models should permit reasonable retraction of commitments while constraining disruptive withdrawals. The analysis treats retraction as necessary both for resolving disputes and for repairing inconsistencies that have been exposed during dialogue.

title: HeterMV: Multi-view reasoning over source-aware heterogeneous evidence graph for multi-source fact verification
abstract: Introduces a source-aware heterogeneous evidence graph for multi-source fact verification, representing core evidence, context, and reference documents as distinct node types. Multi-view reasoning includes an explicit corroboration view and consistency learning intended to combine supportive evidence while suppressing noisy or conflicting signals.

title: Cross-document event ordering through temporal, lexical and distributional knowledge
abstract: Combines event extraction, temporal relations, lexical information, distributional knowledge, and event coreference to order related events across multiple documents.

title: FactBank: a corpus annotated with event factuality
abstract: Introduces a corpus in which event mentions are annotated for factuality as commitments attributed to relevant sources, distinguishing factual, counterfactual, and uncertain assessments rather than assuming that every mentioned event occurred.

title: End-to-end event factuality prediction using directional labeled graph recurrent network
abstract: Presents an end-to-end model that detects event anchors and predicts their factuality jointly using a directional labeled graph recurrent network, reducing dependence on separately supplied event mentions.

title: Document-Level Event Factuality Identification via Reinforced Semantic Learning Network
abstract: Addresses document-level event factuality by selecting relevant sentences and tokens with hierarchical reinforcement learning before encoding the event and its broader document context, rather than relying only on sentence-local cues.
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Utilizing Relative Event Time to Enhance Event-Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Improves event-event temporal relation extraction by explicitly modeling relative event-time information, coupling event timing estimates with relation classification.

title: More than Classification: A Unified Framework for Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Represents temporal relations as logical expressions over event start and end points, unifying extraction under a more compositional temporal representation than a flat multiclass label set.

title: Representing and monitoring social commitments using the event calculus
abstract: Formalizes commitment operations in a first-order Event Calculus with data and metric time and shows how the representation can be used for online monitoring of evolving social commitments.

title: Joint Event and Temporal Relation Extraction with Shared Representations and Structured Prediction
abstract: Jointly detects events and their temporal relations using shared representations and structured prediction, reducing the disconnect between deciding what constitutes an event and reasoning about its temporal placement.

title: Dense Event Ordering with a Multi-Pass Architecture
abstract: Builds dense event-ordering graphs with a multi-pass architecture and uses temporal closure to infer additional relations, supporting document-level temporal structure rather than isolated pair classifications.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: An Improved Neural Baseline for Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Combines contextual neural representations with temporal knowledge and global inference constraints to provide a stronger baseline for extracting event temporal relations.

title: Temporal Information Extraction by Predicting Relative Time-lines
abstract: Represents temporal information by predicting relative positions of event start and end points on a timeline, offering a structured alternative to independent categorical temporal-relation labels.

title: Weakening conflicting information for iterated revision and knowledge integration
abstract: Addresses conflicting information in iterated revision and knowledge integration by weakening inconsistent information rather than simply discarding it, allowing more of the evidence structure to survive conflict resolution.

title: Improving Temporal Relation Extraction with a Globally Acquired Statistical Resource
abstract: Augments local temporal-relation extraction with globally learned event-order statistics and structured inference to improve consistency and robustness of event ordering.
